issues.legal_issue: Whether the classification of transactions as investment or dealing, and the treatment of resulting profits as business profits, is a mixed question of law and fact reviewable by the High Court on a tax reference.
material_facts: The company had held substantial share investments for many years, made relatively few purchases, and disposed of shares in connection with changes in the interests of the group associated with those shares.
The Tribunal classified the company as a dealer, relying in part on its objects and its earlier assertions that it was a dealer.
The dispute concerned the legal effect of the facts found by the Tribunal and whether the profits and losses could be treated as business profits.
issues.conclusion: The classification and tax treatment involve mixed questions of law and fact. The High Court must accept the Tribunal's findings on primary facts but may examine whether the Tribunal applied the relevant legal principles correctly. The Court did not decide the merits of the classification in these appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 66(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a question involving the application of law to facts is reviewable as a question of law. The High Court accepts the Tribunal's primary factual findings but may review its application of the relevant legal principles. The Court relied on G. Venkataswami Naidu & Co. v. C.I.T., 35 I.T.R. 594.

predicates.tax_reference_proceeding: The matter comes before the High Court as a reference arising from a tax assessment dispute.
predicates.tribunal_found_primary_facts: The tribunal made findings about the primary facts underlying the disputed transactions.
predicates.ultimate_classification_requires_legal_p: The ultimate classification of the transactions depends on applying legal principles to the primary facts.

issues.definition: When a tax reference presents primary facts found by the tribunal and an ultimate classification requiring legal principles, the High Court may review the tribunal's application of those principles.

issues.legal_issue: Whether questions framed as asking only whether evidence supports a factual finding adequately present a dispute that turns on the application of law to facts.
material_facts: The company had originally sought reference of questions asking whether it could be treated as a dealer and whether profits and losses from its transactions could be taxed as business profits.
An earlier formulation instead asked whether material supported the finding that the company was a dealer.
The Court concluded that the dispute was mixed law and fact and that the material-support formulation treated it as a question of fact and did not reflect the real controversy.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, the High Court's judgment was set aside, and the Tribunal was directed to make a fresh statement of the case on questions addressing the company's classification and the treatment of its profits and losses.
issues.legal_principle: A reference under sections 66(1) and 66(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, must frame the question to reflect the real legal controversy. Where the dispute is a mixed question of law and fact, a question asking only whether material supports a factual finding is inappropriate; the question should address the legal effect of the facts found.

predicates.appeal_from_high_court_tax_reference: The proceeding is an appeal from a High Court decision on a tax reference.
predicates.referred_question_frames_mixed_issue_as_: The question referred asks whether material supports a finding even though the underlying dispute turns on applying law to facts.
predicates.original_questions_express_actual_contro: The questions originally sought for reference state the substantive dispute that the parties actually raise.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a High Court tax reference concerns a mixed issue framed only as a material-support question, and the original questions express the actual controversy, a fresh statement of the case is directed on properly framed questions.
